findings.claim: Task 1.6 is assigned to livekit-platform and routed R-L (the lead acting in the delivery-lead role), but wr01's declared role list omits livekit-platform, so under the plan's own ownership rule the task's write ownership is undefined; the role lists are unreliable in both directions (wr05 lists design-lead and wr08 lists build-platform with no corresponding tasks).
findings.evidence: Preamble: "Role names are the `.agent-team/know-meet-team` roles; each writes only inside its owned paths." wr01 entry: "- Roles: bdd-quality, design-lead, delivery-lead, build-platform" — yet the task table row is "| wr01 | 1.6 | Verify cluster-context.md against the live cluster, read-only | livekit-platform | WR-3, WR-7 |", and the model row for 1.6 gives "Claude Code, R-L | lead session" where R-L is defined as "the lead session (`claude-fable-5-2`) acting in the delivery-lead role" — three different assignments for one task. Conversely, wr05 declares "Roles: ui-engineer, design-lead" but tasks 5.1–5.4 are all ui-engineer, and wr08 declares "Roles: livekit-platform, build-platform, delivery-lead" but tasks 8.1–8.5 are livekit-platform and 8.6 is delivery-lead.
findings.suggested_fix: Add livekit-platform to wr01's role list (or reassign 1.6 to a listed role and give it a route that matches), and either assign tasks to design-lead in wr05 and build-platform in wr08 or drop them from those changes' role lists.

findings.claim: Operator Batch 1 is scheduled 'before Round 2 starts' although the Round-1 tasks 1.4 and 1.6 depend on it — the task model itself calls the gcloud login 'pre-execution' — so Round 1 (wr01) cannot complete in the order given.
findings.evidence: "**Batch 1, before Round 2 starts:** - Say what the 138 uncommitted changes in the current checkout are, so a clean branch can be cut (task 1.4). ... `gcloud auth login`, so task 1.6 can read the cluster." But the execution order is "Round 1: wr01", which contains tasks 1.4 and 1.6, whose prerequisites are "operator answer on the dirty tree" (1.4) and "gcloud auth login (pre-execution batch)" (1.6). The batch that satisfies Round-1 prerequisites arrives, by the plan's own wording, after Round 1 has started or ended.
findings.suggested_fix: State that Batch 1 is requested once at the phase boundary before Round 1 begins (or at minimum before tasks 1.4 and 1.6 execute), not 'before Round 2 starts'.

findings.claim: The plan's entire acceptance basis — the nine scenarios WR-1 to WR-9, releaseClaim, exclusions, boundaryPacket, budgets and the ownerTask map — lives in adopted-contract.json, which the packet never confirms exists (it is absent from cited_paths while every sibling phase file is confirmed) and whose status is DRAFT with an unstamped digest, so the plan's scenario-coverage claims cannot be checked from the packet.
findings.evidence: Header: "Contract: .kbd-orchestrator/phases/web-release/adopted-contract.json / status DRAFT, not adopted; digest is stamped by the adoption writer"; "The contract's `releaseClaim`, `exclusions` and nine scenarios (WR-1 to WR-9) are the acceptance; this file orders the work that reaches them"; "The map is the `ownerTask` field of each scenario in the contract." cited_paths confirms cluster-context.md, decision-log.md, library-candidates.json, method-context.md, prior-context.md and versions.toml under .kbd-orchestrator/phases/web-release — but not adopted-contract.json, so no packet artifact defines what WR-1..WR-9 actually assert.
findings.suggested_fix: Inline or attach the draft contract's scenario list (IDs, statements, ownerTask) in the plan, and confirm adopted-contract.json exists on disk before adoption is requested.
